title: City land for affordable housing at University Avenue
subtitle: Also: 2024 tax levy, road resurfacing funding, Waterloo Park, Grey Silo lease, and a church daycare rezoning.
overview: Council voted to move ahead with plans to use the city-owned site at 2025 University Ave E for housing {{vote:m5}}. The land is zoned for employment. Staff will run further public engagement and then report back on a possible Modified Ministerial Zoning Order. The aim is a mixed-income community with affordable, attainable and market housing. Staff said the site could hold roughly 700 units, and a builder would be chosen later through a request for proposals.

Council also adopted the 2024 general tax levy {{vote:m6}} and released capital funding for road resurfacing across 2024 to 2026 {{vote:m10}}. It released funds for Waterloo Park master plan work {{vote:m9}} and approved a renewal of the Grey Silo golf course lease {{vote:m11}}. A zoning change for 275 Erb Street East will allow a child care centre and private school inside an existing church {{vote:m12}}.

Council held a closed meeting on a shelter update. The minutes report no decisions from it. Council also heard that staff are researching tools to address renovictions and demovictions as part of the rental housing by-law review, with more to come in the coming months.

decisions.detail: Council directed staff to proceed with further engagement on using 2025 University Ave E for residential purposes and acknowledged the proposed Modified Ministerial Zoning Order process {{vote:m5}}.
Council approved the report and adopted the 2024 General Levy By-law based on a final municipal levy of $99,609,666 {{vote:m6}}.
Council released $2,124,000 now, and $1,663,000 in 2025 and $1,538,000 in 2026, for road resurfacing from the Capital Infrastructure Reinvestment Reserve Fund {{vote:m10}}.
Council released $564,000 in 2024 non-routine capital funding for the Waterloo Park Master Plan implementation project {{vote:m9}}.
Council approved renewing the lease with GolfNorth Management Corp. for the Grey Silo Golf Course and authorized the Mayor and Clerk to sign it {{vote:m11}}.
Council approved Zoning By-law Amendment Z-24-06 to add a child care centre and private school to the existing church site {{vote:m12}}.
Council approved amended Banner, Program Refund and Withdrawal, and Advertising and Sponsorship policies {{vote:m8}}.
Council approved report COM2024-018 and authorized the Mayor to sign the Multi-Sector Service Accountability Agreement declaration and related documents {{vote:m2}}.

debate: Staff and the Mayor argued that waiting for the Region's regular employment-land review could take many years during a housing crisis. They said a ministerial zoning order would speed up the process without skipping public engagement.

Councillors asked about public consultation. Staff proposed posting the report on the city's engagement site, contacting neighbourhood associations and Indigenous communities, and holding an in-person public meeting. One councillor suggested a city-wide location rather than only the local ward.

On the loss of employment land, staff said the site is mainly suited to office and light industrial use and has drawn no interest in past offerings. Staff also noted it is the city's largest industrial parcel, so the decision has long-term implications once the west-side employment lands are built out.

One councillor asked whether denser options than the assumed four to six storeys should be tested with developers, since the zoning order would fix what can be built. Staff said they would consult developers and might add flexibility to the draft by-law.

A delegate presented a remote-controlled boat that removes floating debris from lakes, and staff were asked to connect with the delegate. Councillors asked about lighting on the southwest side of Waterloo Park, and staff said it could be reviewed through future projects and the broader master plan.
